title: Contrastive Representation Regularization for Vision-Language-Action Models
claim: A lightweight auxiliary contrastive path, supervised by soft state similarity, can be added to a standard model's training pipeline.
layout: 2 regions, bottom-to-top then right, dashed line to decoder, nested boxes
description: A block diagram of a vision-language-action training pipeline. At the bottom left are three camera views (one outlined in red dotted) and a text instruction, "Open the Cabinet Door". They pass upward through a frozen pre-trained Vision-Language Model (snowflake icon) into rows of blue image tokens and beige text tokens. A second token row has a few grayed, red-dotted tokens, which shows the view cutoff. Both rows feed a trainable Adapter (flame icon). Pink tokens go from the Adapter to a Projector at top. A panel labeled (b) "Robot State-aware Contrastive Loss" sits at right. It shows similar and dissimilar robot-state samples linked by arrows, with pink for similar and light purple for dissimilar. A dashed line carries the adapted embeddings down to an Action Decoder (e.g., DiT), which outputs control actions to a real robot photo.
caption: Overview. We extend the standard VLA model training framework with a contrastive regularization path. Embeddings from the pre-trained VLM are augmented by the view cutoff operation applied on the feature slice corresponding to a randomly selected observation view, and are optimized with our Robot State-aware Contrastive Loss to attract samples with similar proprioceptive states.
abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have shown strong capabilities in robot manipulation by leveraging rich representations from pre-trained Vision-Language Models (VLMs). However, their representations arguably remain suboptimal, lacking sensitivity to robotic signals such as control actions and proprioceptive information. To address the issue, we introduce Robot State-aware Contrastive Loss (RS-CL), a simple and effective representation regularization for VLA models, designed to bridge the gap between VLM representations and robotic signals. In particular, RS-CL aligns the representations more closely with the robot's proprioceptive states by using relative distances between the states as soft supervision. Complementing the original action prediction objective, RS-CL enhances control-relevant representation learning, while being lightweight and fully compatible with standard VLA training pipelines. Our empirical results demonstrate that RS-CL substantially improves the performance of state-of-the-art VLA models; it pushes the prior art to 69.7% achieving the state-of-the-art performance on the RoboCasa-Kitchen benchmark, and boosts success rates from 45.0% to 58.3% on challenging real-robot manipulation tasks.
